evidence.quote:
“Residential dwelling unit” means any house, apartment,
accessory unit, or other unit intended to be used as a primary residence in the
State. “Residential dwelling unit” shall not include inpatient medical care,
licensed long-term care, or detention or correctional facilities.

(1)   collecting the competitively sensitive
information of two or more rental property owners for the purpose of analyzing
or processing information through the use of an algorithm or other automated
process, including by using the information to train an algorithm, where the
algorithm or other automated process is used to set or recommend rental prices,
material lease terms, or occupancy levels;
e.     any person to perform a coordinating function.

“Rental
property owner” means a person that owns, directly or indirectly, one or more
rental residential dwelling units.  Any person that holds a controlling
interest in an entity that owns a rental residential dwelling unit shall be
deemed to constitute a single rental property owner with that entity.
1

“Competitively
sensitive information” means nonpublic information including, but not limited
to, prices, supply levels, security deposits, ideal occupancy levels, lease
contract termination, renewal dates of residential dwelling units, or any other
material lease terms.

“Nonpublic information” means information that is not
available to the public at no cost. In instances where the information is
combined with public information, all combined information shall be deemed
nonpublic information.

(2)   setting rental prices, material lease terms, or
occupancy levels pursuant to an underlying algorithm or other automated process
that analyzes or processes competitively sensitive information of any other
rental property owner, including by using that competitively sensitive
information to train an algorithm; or

(3)   setting for or recommending to two or more rental
property owners: rental prices, material lease terms, or occupancy levels
pursuant to the same or a substantially similar underlying algorithm or other
automated process, that facilitates parallel pricing coordination.

“Parallel pricing coordination” means a tacit or
express agreement between two or more rental property owners to raise, change,
maintain, or manipulate pricing for the leasing of reasonably interchangeable
residential dwelling units, unless required to do so in accordance with
affordability controls.  This includes agreements between a coordinator and
multiple property owners.
1

“Tacit agreement” means mutual consent demonstrated
without verbal or written communication.  Mutual consent may, but need not, be
demonstrated by a pattern of conduct.

Current expression supersedes historical uncompiled-coverage descriptions only for the selected factual gates. Original review issues are retained for audit; remaining unsupported paths are enumerated in verification.json.

One actor, one activity or service transaction, a documented owner/principal mapping, associated datasets/processes/recipients, and an as-of date. Do not combine facts from unrelated activities to complete a branch.

All existing coordinating-function research, free-estimate, brokerage and governmental exclusions apply to that same selected activity. A provider with an excluded estimate activity may also conduct a nonexcluded coordinating function. Keep original paid exemptions unchanged in this bounded increment, with unresolved coordinator exemptions retained.

Controlling-interest holder and the entity it controls constitute a single owner. Map direct/indirect rental ownership first; do not substitute person count, accounts, legal-entity count, unit count or recipient count for collected-owner count. Complex shared-control/transitive mapping needs legal review; this design adds no ownership-normalization engine.
Apply to the same selected dataset; mixtures containing nonpublic information are nonpublic. Examples are nonexhaustive. Unknown category or access facts stay null.

Do not require competitively sensitive or nonpublic information for branch 3; its text contains no such condition. Same-process identity can satisfy the first similarity alternative but cannot settle parallel pricing coordination.

Remove inherited residential fact from both selected coverage expressions. Registry residential describes actual use, whereas the statute defines intended primary residence. Retain intended_primary_residence, existing NJ jurisdiction routing, facility exclusions and expressly rental-related owner/conduct fields. Vacancy or current residential=false must not independently exclude intended-primary-residence rental units.

Conduct booleans distinguish rental prices/occupancy from lease terms. If only lease terms are involved and materiality is unresolved, input must remain null and review dependency persists. Do not encode analyst confidence as a legal conclusion or infer materiality from software use.
Incomplete owner mapping never becomes zero; absent conduct never becomes false; disputed legal characterization remains unknown. Supplemental input registration remains a Platform dependency.

args.reason: The actor must be the qualifying owner or its agent, representative or subcontractor, and the identified service provider must satisfy the operative coordinator/software-or-device/coordinating-function definition and scoped exclusions. Owner units and a service action do not settle these uncompiled relationships and legal qualifications.

evidence.quote:
“Residential dwelling unit” means any house, apartment,
accessory unit, or other unit intended to be used as a primary residence in the
State. “Residential dwelling unit” shall not include inpatient medical care,
licensed long-term care, or detention or correctional facilities.

“Rental
property owner” means a person that owns, directly or indirectly, one or more
rental residential dwelling units.  Any person that holds a controlling
interest in an entity that owns a rental residential dwelling unit shall be
deemed to constitute a single rental property owner with that entity.
1

“Coordinator” means any person who operates
1
[
a software or
data analytics service
]
algorithmic revenue management software or an algorithmic device
1
that
performs a coordinating function for any rental property owner, including a
rental property owner performing a coordinating function for their own benefit.
“Coordinator” shall not include a government entity that sets or limits rents
or sale prices of residential property through affordability controls in
accordance with law.

“Coordinating function” shall not include the following:
(1)
providing, using, or collecting competitively sensitive
information solely for the purpose of conducting
research, statistical analysis, or testing, where the competitively
sensitive information is not used in setting or recommending rental prices,
material lease terms, fees, occupancy rates or levels, or other contract terms
for current or future leases;
(2)
developing an estimated amount of rent that is
made available to the public at no cost;
(3)
the use of a real estate brokerage database that is available on
equal terms to subscribers that lists properties for rent or sale but does not:
(a) set or recommend rental prices, material lease
terms, or occupancy rates or levels; or
(b) collect competitively sensitive information to set or
recommend rental prices, material lease terms, or occupancy rates or levels; or
(4)   a government entity setting or limiting rents or
sale prices of residential property through affordability controls in
accordance with the law.
